slides.title: Confidentiality
slides.teach: Confidentiality means keeping information private from people who are not authorized to see it.

course.learn: Confidentiality means keeping information private from people who are not authorized to see it.

breakdown.explanation: Only approved people should be able to see sensitive information.
Encryption, passwords, MFA, file permissions, and access controls.

course.why: Unauthorized disclosure can expose credentials, personal data, financial records, and other sensitive information.
course.example: An employee accidentally sends customer Social Security numbers to the wrong recipient.
course.exam: If the scenario emphasizes exposure, disclosure, unauthorized viewing, or leaked information, think confidentiality.
course.check_q: A hacker reads unencrypted employee credentials. Which CIA principle is affected?

slides.title: Integrity
slides.teach: Integrity means keeping information accurate and protected from unauthorized changes.

course.learn: Integrity means keeping information accurate and protected from unauthorized changes.

breakdown.explanation: The data should remain correct and trustworthy.
Hashing, digital signatures, checksums, permissions, and version controls.

course.why: Security decisions can become unreliable if data is altered without authorization.
course.example: An attacker changes employees' direct-deposit bank account numbers in payroll.
course.exam: If data was modified, altered, tampered with, or can no longer be trusted, think integrity.
course.check_q: Malware modifies financial records without permission. Which CIA principle is affected?

slides.title: Availability
slides.teach: Availability means making sure authorized users can access systems and data when needed.

course.learn: Availability means making sure authorized users can access systems and data when needed.

breakdown.explanation: The system must be usable when legitimate users need it.
Backups, redundancy, failover, disaster recovery, load balancing, and UPS systems.

course.why: A secure system still fails its users if it is unavailable when needed.
course.example: A DDoS attack overwhelms a website so legitimate customers cannot connect.
course.exam: If users cannot access a system, application, service, or data, think availability.
course.check_q: A database server fails and employees cannot access records. Which CIA principle is affected?

questions.q: A stolen laptop contains unencrypted customer records. Which CIA principle is MOST directly at risk?
questions.explanation: Confidentiality is concerned with preventing unauthorized disclosure of information.

questions.q: An attacker changes employees' direct-deposit information in a payroll database. Which CIA principle is compromised?
questions.explanation: Integrity is affected because the data was modified without authorization.

questions.q: A DDoS attack prevents customers from reaching a company's website. Which CIA principle is MOST affected?
questions.explanation: Availability is affected because legitimate users cannot access the service.

questions.q: A hacker intercepts unencrypted traffic and reads employee credentials. Which CIA principle is MOST directly affected?
questions.explanation: The information was exposed to an unauthorized party, which is a confidentiality issue.

questions.q: Malware modifies financial records but the database remains online. Which CIA principle is MOST directly affected?
questions.explanation: The key issue is unauthorized modification of data, which affects integrity.
